Member (Liam Cote): The pharmacy said my new prescription needs another form before you'll cover it.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Hi Liam Cote, Chloe Gagnon here — let me pull that up.
Member (Liam Cote): I uploaded the prescription through the app already.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Liam Cote): Yes, that's right.
Member (Liam Cote): My doctor charges 45 dollars to fill in forms.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Which medication or service is the request about?
Member (Liam Cote): A new medication my specialist started me on last week.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Did the pharmacy give you the name of the form they need?
Member (Liam Cote): They said 'prior authorization' and gave me a number to call. That's it.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Which pharmacy are you using?
Member (Liam Cote): The one near my work. They said they can resubmit as soon as it's approved.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): How much medication do you have left?

Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Let me take a look. I've checked the information request and the documents already on file.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): For this medication the plan needs a prior authorization from your doctor, not just the prescription.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I'm checking whether anything from your doctor's office is already on file.
Member (Liam Cote): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): The prior authorization form is on file from last week. It just wasn't linked to the drug claim. I've linked it, and the pharmacy can resubmit today.
Member (Liam Cote): So I can pick it up today?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Yes. The authorization is linked to the claim now, so the pharmacy can resubmit and it should go through.
Member (Liam Cote): Will I have to do this every time?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): No. It's approved for twelve months, so refills go through automatically.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): So you're all set: the authorization is on file for twelve months and the pharmacy can process it today.
Member (Liam Cote): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Lucas Roy): I've been off work for six weeks and still haven't had a decision on my short-term disability claim.

Member (Lucas Roy): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): When did you go off work?
Member (Lucas Roy): Six weeks ago. I submitted my part in the first week.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Do you know roughly when HR sent their statement?
Member (Lucas Roy): They said about three weeks ago, but I haven't seen anything confirming it.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Is there a good number and time to reach you?

Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Are you receiving any other income right now, like sick days from work?
Member (Lucas Roy): My sick days ran out two weeks ago.

Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Your file has your statement and your doctor's statement. I'm checking whether the employer's statement has come in.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Once the file is complete, the case manager makes the decision and calls you to explain it.

Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.

Member (Lucas Roy): So when does the first payment come?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): It's scheduled for Friday, and it includes the weeks since your waiting period ended.
Member (Lucas Roy): Who do I contact if something changes?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Your case manager is Denise. I've sent you her direct line by secure message.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): To recap: your claim is approved, the first payment is Friday, and Denise will call this week about your return-to-work plan.
Member (Lucas Roy): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Emma Fortin): My dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Hi Emma Fortin, Marc Tremblay here — let me pull that up.
Member (Emma Fortin): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Emma Fortin): Yes, that's right.
Member (Emma Fortin): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Which procedure was the request for?
Member (Emma Fortin): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Is this the first request or a resubmission?
Member (Emma Fortin): The second. The first was denied in July.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Has the dental office called us about this directly?
Member (Emma Fortin): They said they called and got the same answer as me.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Are you in any pain right now?
Member (Emma Fortin): Some. It's manageable, but I can't chew on that side.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the pre-authorization request and the documents received from the dental office.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): The assessment is done against the plan's criteria for crowns, which are set by Health Canada.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I'm looking at the latest assessment on your file now.
Member (Emma Fortin): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): The first request was missing the radiograph date. The second one is complete and has been assessed, and it's approved. Your dentist will get the confirmation today.
Member (Emma Fortin): So the crown is covered now?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Yes. It's approved at your plan's coverage level, and your dentist will get the confirmation today.
Member (Emma Fortin): Do I pay anything?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): That depends on your co-payment level. Your dentist will see it on the confirmation.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): To recap: the crown is approved, and your dentist will get the confirmation today with your co-payment.
Member (Emma Fortin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-000108.transcript:
Member (Mathieu Roy): I asked to transfer my pension from my old employer's plan to my bank and it still hasn't moved.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Hi Mathieu Roy, Aisha Rahman here — let me pull that up.
Member (Mathieu Roy): The market's moved since then and I've lost money waiting.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Mathieu Roy): Yes, that's right.
Member (Mathieu Roy): The receiving institution says they never got anything.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Where is the money going?
Member (Mathieu Roy): To an RRSP at my bank. They say they're waiting on Sun Life.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): When did you send in the transfer request?
Member (Mathieu Roy): In June. I signed everything they sent me.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Did the bank send you a transfer form to sign as well?
Member (Mathieu Roy): I think so. They handled their side.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Have you received any statement showing the transfer as pending?
Member (Mathieu Roy): Only the annual statement, which still shows the balance with you.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Let me take a look. I've traced the transfer request and the paperwork on the plan account.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Your request came in on June 14. The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer authorization from the receiving institution, which is standard for locked-in pension money.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Until that form arrives, the funds stay invested in your current options, so they've moved with the market.
Member (Mathieu Roy): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): The transfer was held because the receiving institution's form wasn't signed. It came in this morning, so I've released it, and the funds will move within five business days.
Member (Mathieu Roy): So it's finally moving?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Yes. The form arrived this morning, and I've released the transfer.
Member (Mathieu Roy): How long until my bank has it?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Usually five business days, and you'll get a confirmation letter from us.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): So the transfer is released and should reach your bank within five business days.
Member (Mathieu Roy): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-000204.transcript:
Member (Emma Fortin): My dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Emma Fortin, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.
Member (Emma Fortin): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Emma Fortin): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Emma Fortin): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Emma Fortin): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Emma Fortin): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Emma Fortin): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Emma Fortin): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with your previous paid claims and the plan booklet.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Emma Fortin): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Emma Fortin): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Emma Fortin): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Emma Fortin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Fatima Chen): Great, that helps.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): I'll also send the coordination-of-benefits form for your spouse's plan.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): So, 50% up to 2,500 dollars, a pre-determination first, and your spouse's plan can cover part of the rest.

SL-001688.transcript:
Member (Mei Fortin): My dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Hi Mei Fortin, Kevin Nguyen here — let me pull that up.
Member (Mei Fortin): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Mei Fortin): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Mei Fortin): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Mei Fortin): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Mei Fortin): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Mei Fortin): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Mei Fortin): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with your previous paid claims and the plan booklet.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Mei Fortin): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Mei Fortin): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Mei Fortin): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Mei Fortin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Mathieu Kim): My son needs braces and I want to know what my plan pays before we commit.

SL-002982.transcript:
Member (Leila Morrison): I'm following up again — I'm waiting on a decision on my disability claim and nobody has called me.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Leila Morrison, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Leila Morrison): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Leila Morrison): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Leila Morrison): Yes, that's right.
Member (Leila Morrison): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Do you know roughly when HR sent their statement?
Member (Leila Morrison): They said about three weeks ago, but I haven't seen anything confirming it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Is there a good number and time to reach you?
Member (Leila Morrison): My mobile, any time before three. I have appointments in the afternoons.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Are you receiving any other income right now, like sick days from work?
Member (Leila Morrison): My sick days ran out two weeks ago.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the disability file and the case manager's task list.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Your file has your statement and your doctor's statement. I'm checking whether the employer's statement has come in.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Once the file is complete, the case manager makes the decision and calls you to explain it.
Member (Leila Morrison): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): The file is still waiting on the employer's statement. I've flagged it to your case manager, but I can't make a decision on the claim from here.
Member (Leila Morrison): So I'm still waiting with no income?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I know that's hard. I've marked the file as a priority because you have no other income right now.
Member (Leila Morrison): Is there anything I can do to speed it up?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Ask HR for the date they sent the statement. If it's missing, that's the one thing holding the file.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: the file is waiting on the employer's statement, your case manager has been asked to call you, and I've noted your preferred contact times.
Member (Leila Morrison): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.
